tdlr._phone_note: Enforcement handles the CHEL. Customer Service reps CANNOT answer questions about ENF006/ENF003. Point users at Enforcement.

mailing_address.line1: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation

tdlr.fee_note: Per LICENSE TYPE, not per crime. Cashier's check or money order payable to TDLR. NOT cash.

get_your_record._CRITICAL: There are TWO paths and the cheap one CAN LOSE YOU THE CASE. Steer users to the FINGERPRINT review. A name-based search can silently miss a conviction -- which is the exact omission that voids the evaluation letter.

RECOMMENDED_fingerprint_personal_review.label: Texas DPS — Personal Review of your complete criminal history (fingerprint-based)
RECOMMENDED_fingerprint_personal_review.cost_breakdown: $10 fingerprint capture at IdentoGO + $15 for the criminal history record
RECOMMENDED_fingerprint_personal_review.turnaround: typically days (mail results can take ~10 business days)
RECOMMENDED_fingerprint_personal_review.why: This is your COMPLETE Texas record, including arrests that did not lead to conviction. Fingerprints positively identify you. Nothing gets missed because of a name spelling.

NOT_RECOMMENDED_name_search.label: DPS public name-based conviction search
NOT_RECOMMENDED_name_search.why_not: DPS itself warns: 'The only way to positively link someone to a criminal record is through fingerprint identification.' A name search uses Soundex matching -- it CAN MISS your records and CAN return someone else's. It also only shows convictions and deferred adjudications (Gov't Code §411.135). A missed conviction voids the TDLR letter.
NOT_RECOMMENDED_name_search.surepath_position: Mention it exists, and say plainly why it is the wrong tool for this. Do not link it as the primary path.

out_of_state_and_federal.label: FBI — Identity History Summary Check
out_of_state_and_federal.verify_note: VERIFY THE URL AND THE CURRENT FEE BEFORE THE DEMO.
out_of_state_and_federal.why: The Texas DPS record shows TEXAS. TDLR requires you report in-state, out-of-state, AND federal offenses. This is the only way to see the rest.

cant_remember_the_court.label: Texas county and district clerks
cant_remember_the_court.guidance: TDLR's own FAQ says: call the COUNTY clerk for misdemeanors, the DISTRICT clerk for felonies, in the county where it happened.

expungement_and_nondisclosure._INVARIANT: CLAUDE.md L8 — SurePath NEVER advises whether an expunged or sealed record must be disclosed. We present the information. The USER decides, with TDLR or a lawyer.
what_the_sources_say: EXPUNCTION destroys the record. The person may generally deny it occurred.
An ORDER OF NONDISCLOSURE seals the record from the PUBLIC, but it REMAINS AVAILABLE to certain government and licensing agencies.
Nondisclosure is most commonly granted after DEFERRED ADJUDICATION — which TDLR explicitly REQUIRES be reported.
TDLR's published FAQ addresses NEITHER expunction nor nondisclosure.
expungement_and_nondisclosure.surepath_copy: We can't tell you whether an expunged or sealed record has to be disclosed. Expunction and an order of nondisclosure are different things, and the answer is different for each. This is a question for TDLR or a lawyer — ask before you decide.
expungement_and_nondisclosure.status: OPEN — see OPEN_QUESTIONS.md Q8. Pending written answer from TDLR Enforcement.

chel_authority.cite: Tex. Occ. Code §51.4012 and ch. 53, subch. D
chel_authority.what: Authorizes the pre-application criminal history evaluation letter.

factors_considered.what: The factors TDLR weighs: extent and nature of past criminal activity; age when the crime was committed; time elapsed since; conduct and work activity before and after; evidence of rehabilitation; other evidence of fitness including letters of recommendation.
use_on: Stage 4 (Your story) — the STATIC coaching copy. Quote it. Cite it. CLAUDE.md L5.

public_criminal_history.what: Defines what the DPS public name search shows — convictions and deferred adjudications only.

tdlr_faq_panel._purpose: TDLR published 16 FAQs. They are the STATE'S OWN WORDS on the state's own site — scrivener-safe, quotable, citable. Surface them as expandable panels RIGHT WHERE THE QUESTION ARISES, not buried on a help page.
place_near_record_intake: What crimes do I have to report?
I got a deferred adjudication and was technically not convicted. Do I still report it?
How many years back do I go? Do I report convictions older than ten years?
What if I can't remember all my crimes?
What if I can't remember the date, or which court?
Do I have to report a DWI? Isn't that a traffic violation?

What does 'crimes which relate to the occupation' mean?
place_near_review: When will I get a response?

You said no — can I apply anyway?
rules: Paraphrase TDLR's answers. Attribute them to TDLR. Link to the source.
The expungement/nondisclosure entry is OURS, not TDLR's, and must be marked as an open question (L8).
